clue.text: Dawn chorus taking centre stage, enriching air

indicators.note: something added to enrich the air goes into it, so the centre letters sit inside the word for air

parts.note: an air or aura is a distinctive atmosphere about someone

indicators.note: only the central letters of the word chorus are taken

explanation.surface: Birds singing at daybreak take over and fill the morning air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawn chorus' looks like one phrase, but 'Dawn' alone is the definition; 'chorus' supplies only its two middle letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aurora is the Latin name for the goddess of the dawn, and the word is used poetically for daybreak.

clue.text: After vacation in Argyll, one learned to gut marine fish

indicators.note: the graduate and the gutting come after the emptied place name
vacating the inside of the place name empties it, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate, someone learned
to core is to remove the inside, as with an apple

explanation.surface: A scholar holidaying in the Scottish west coast region learns to clean a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacation in' Argyll leaves AL; 'one learned' is BA, a degree holder. Argyll is a region of western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned tuna found in the open ocean, so it is a sea fish.

clue.text: Wild spree, primarily collecting furniture that's decent

indicators.note: wild suggests disorder, so the letters of spree are scrambled
primarily means first of all, so only the first letter of collecting is used

parts.note: a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A shopping spree buying antique furniture turns out to be perfectly respectable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges SPREE into RESPE; 'primarily' takes C from 'collecting'; 'that's' only links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectable and decent both describe conduct that is proper and socially acceptable: they are synonyms.

clue.text: Culinary mixture, interlinking game and beef

indicators.note: interlinking the two short words weaves their letters together, so they are rearranged into a new order

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, the game
an ox is a beef animal; beef comes from oxen

explanation.surface: A cookery note about a sauce base combining venison and beef.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of RU and OX alternate, R-O-U-X, one from each word in turn; the grammar treats this interleaving as a rearrangement. 'game' looks like meat beside 'beef' but is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A roux is cooked flour and fat, the base for sauces such as béchamel, so it is a kitchen blend.

clue.text: Daughter in parachute gear, tough character

indicators.note: the abbreviation for daughter goes inside the word for the straps

parts.note: a parachute is worn on a harness of straps
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A girl strapped into her parachute harness shows she is a tough nut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside HARNESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardness is the quality of being hard or tough, here read as a toughness of character.

clue.text: Former aristocrat's curv'd string instrument shortened

parts.note: arch'd, poetically clipped like the clue's own word, means curved into an arch

indicators.note: the instrument's name is cut down to its familiar short form

parts.note: the ukulele is a small four-stringed guitar

explanation.surface: A noble from history plays a curved stringed instrument, cut down in size.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'curv'd' hints that ARCH'D is clipped the same way. 'shortened' turns UKULELE into its everyday short form UKE. The 's' after 'aristocrat' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archduke was a prince of the Habsburg Austrian imperial family, a title no longer held in practice.

clue.text: Assume British promoter's wanting top cricketer

parts.note: to don clothing is to put it on, to assume it
an adman promotes products through advertising

explanation.surface: An imagined British sports promoter is short of a star cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assume' looks like a verb of supposing, but here it means to put on. Don Bradman was the Australian batsman with a Test average of 99.94, widely seen as cricket's greatest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Don Bradman is generally regarded as the finest batsman ever to play Test cricket.

clue.text: 24 are standing

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing upright means the word is written from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that reads like a figure of people being on their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'standing' sends ARE up the down light, giving ERA. The answer to 24 is CRETACEOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretaceous is a span of geological time, loosely an era of Earth's history.

clue.text: Husband splits gingery drink

indicators.note: the abbreviation for husband splits the colour word in two by going inside it

parts.note: sandy describes hair of a light ginger or yellowish-red colour

explanation.surface: A husband divides a ginger beer drink with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splits' puts H inside SANDY. 'gingery drink' suggests ginger beer, but 'gingery' is the colour. Shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Shandy is a drink of beer mixed with lemonade or ginger beer.

clue.text: Drone thus half-hidden over Scottish Island

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the first piece sits above the second
half of the word thus is hidden, leaving its first two letters showing

parts.note: Rum is an island of the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A buzzing aircraft, partly out of sight, passes over a Hebridean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hidden' leaves TH of THUS; 'over' puts it above RUM, an island off western Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: To thrum is to make a continuous low humming or strumming sound, the same idea as a drone.

clue.text: Metal body part put back to front in error

indicators.note: the turned body part goes inside the slang word for a blunder

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

indicators.note: back to front means the word for the body part is read in reverse

parts.note: tum is an informal word for the stomach

explanation.surface: A metallic body part fitted the wrong way round by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back to front' gives MUT. 'bish' is dated British slang for a blunder, and 'tum' is a childish word for the stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismuth is a brittle chemical element classed among the metals, number 83 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Musical piece from John so long

parts.note: john and can are both slang for a toilet
ta-ta is an informal British goodbye, like so long

explanation.surface: Someone called John offers a piece of music as a farewell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a name, perhaps a composer, but is slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a sung composition for voices and instruments, as Bach wrote, so a work of music.

clue.text: One works with chow, playing fetch when temperature dropped

indicators.note: playing about with the letters rearranges them
dropped means the letter for temperature is left out

explanation.surface: A chow dog playing fetch once the weather cools down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped' takes T out of FETCH, and 'playing' rearranges FECH. 'chow' looks like the dog breed that would play fetch, but means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Chow is slang for food, and a chef is a professional cook who works with it.

clue.text: Special child sedated, getting blood in empty ward

indicators.note: the sedated word and the family word go inside the emptied ward
an empty ward has its inside letters removed, leaving only the first and last

parts.note: under means unconscious, as under anaesthetic
kin, like blood, means one's relatives

explanation.surface: A gifted child is sedated and given a transfusion in an empty hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blood' looks medical beside 'sedated', but means family, as in 'kith and kin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wunderkind, German for wonder child, is a prodigy, a child of exceptional talent.

clue.text: Search sink unit opening

parts.note: to sink money into something is to invest it
I is the Roman numeral for one, a unit
a gate is an opening in a wall or fence

explanation.surface: A plumber checks the cupboard opening under the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sink unit' reads as a kitchen fitting, but 'sink' is a verb meaning invest and 'unit' is the number one.
explanation.definitionFit: To investigate is to examine or inquire into something closely, in effect to search.

clue.text: Nasty crashing of plane captured by American worker

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are held inside the abbreviation for American
a crashing plane is wrecked, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: the worker ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A grim account of a plane crash investigated by an American labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashing' turns the letters of 'plane' into NPLEA, which 'captured by' then holds inside the abbreviation for American.
explanation.definitionFit: Unpleasant and nasty are synonyms, both meaning disagreeable or offensive.

clue.text: Keep, with article moving rearmost, section of Observer?

indicators.note: the article is shifted to the very end of the word for keep

parts.note: to keep something is to retain it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor shifts an article to the back pages of The Observer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving rearmost' shifts A in RETAIN to the end. 'Observer' looks like the British Sunday newspaper, but is an eye; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The retina is the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye, a part of anyone who observes.

clue.text: Perform high jump, sidestep about three feet

indicators.note: about means the word for dodging goes around the measure

parts.note: to skive is British slang for dodging work or duty
a yard, abbreviated YD, is three feet

explanation.surface: An athlete in the high jump dodges sideways around a three-foot bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high jump' suggests the athletics event, but it is a jump from an aircraft. 'Skive' is British slang for dodging work.
explanation.definitionFit: To skydive is to jump from an aircraft and freefall before opening a parachute, a very high leap.

clue.text: Rocky piece to record again without REM band name

indicators.note: without means those three letters are removed from the recording word

parts.note: to remaster is to make a new master recording
O is a ring shape, a band
ID, identification, gives one's name

explanation.surface: Re-recording a rock song without the band REM's name on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes REM out of REMASTER, leaving ASTER. 'Rocky piece' and 'REM band' suggest rock music; REM is the American rock group.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a rocky body orbiting the Sun, a fragment of rock in space.

clue.text: Zero concession available screening superior comedy film

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket

indicators.note: screening means the concession word hides the letter for superior inside it

parts.note: a sop is a concession offered to placate someone
U stands for upper class, superior

explanation.surface: A cinema offers no concessions while screening a top-notch comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screening' looks like a cinema word but puts SOP round U. Duck Soup is the 1933 Marx Brothers film; a duck is a cricket score of nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Duck Soup is a 1933 Marx Brothers film, a classic of screen comedy.

clue.text: Column of deer eating remains beyond Asian river

indicators.note: beyond means the deer comes after the river in the answer

parts.note: the Ob is a great river of Siberia

indicators.note: eating means the deer word swallows the verb meaning remains

parts.note: the elk is a large deer
is, as in 'remains' or 'exists', the verb to be

explanation.surface: A herd of deer feeding on remains beyond an Asian river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' looks like a noun, leftovers, but is a verb: something that remains simply is.
explanation.definitionFit: An obelisk is a tall tapering stone pillar, a kind of column or monument.

clue.text: Known as sauce bottling site in Caribbean

indicators.note: the phrase bottles the answer, holding it inside its letters

explanation.surface: A place renowned for bottling its sauce, somewhere in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottling' signals the answer is held within 'Known as sauce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nassau is the capital of the Bahamas, an island nation in the Caribbean region.

clue.text: Hand beginning to spoil stroke in pool

indicators.note: the beginning of spoil is its first letter

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke

explanation.surface: A swimmer begins to spoil their swimming stroke in the pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' here means handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand can mean handwriting, and a scrawl is untidy, hurried handwriting.

clue.text: Court attendant Jack joins public indignation as case dismissed

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in playing cards

indicators.note: the case is the outside, so the first and last letters are dismissed

parts.note: a furore is an outbreak of public anger

explanation.surface: Jack joins the public outrage when the court case is thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as case dismissed' removes the outer letters F and E from FURORE, the British spelling. 'case dismissed' reads as legal language, but strips the word's outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A juror is a member of a jury, someone who attends court to hear a trial.

clue.text: Criminal court case covering drug period

indicators.note: the jumbled letters cover, or enclose, the drug letter
criminal suggests something crooked, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A criminal court case about drug dealing over some length of time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges COURT CASE, and 'covering' puts that round E. 'period' looks like a prison term, but is geological.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cretaceous is the geological period ending about 66 million years ago with the dinosaurs.

clue.text: Vacuous Nick on Love Island that sounds like a swine

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing on another comes after it, so the emptied name follows the two letters

parts.note: love is a score of zero in tennis, written O

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the middle of the name is removed, leaving the outer letters

explanation.surface: An empty-headed contestant on the TV show Love Island behaves like a pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love Island' is a British reality dating show; here it splits into O and I.
explanation.definitionFit: Oink is the grunting noise a pig makes, so it is the swine's call.

clue.text: Unknown delivery time character in Argos revealed

parts.note: z is used as an unknown in algebra
ETA, estimated time of arrival, is when a delivery is due

explanation.surface: An Argos order shows an unknown delivery time.
explanation.walkthrough: Argos is a British catalogue retailer and also a city in ancient Greece, where the letters are Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeta is the sixth letter of the Greek alphabet, so a character used in a Greek city.

clue.text: Fruit business recruits endlessly talkative

indicators.note: the word for fuss takes the trimmed word into its ranks, enclosing it

parts.note: ado is fuss or business, as in 'without further ado'

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: vocal means outspoken, talkative

explanation.surface: A fruit company hires staff who never stop talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves VOCA from the word for talkative.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree.

clue.text: Faceless yob banned

indicators.note: with its face, the front, removed the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a lout is a yob, a boorish young man

explanation.surface: An anonymous thug is banned from the premises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faceless' removes the first letter of LOUT. A yob is British slang for a loutish youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Out can mean not allowed or forbidden, as in 'smoking indoors is out'.

clue.text: Geordie to go probing sandwich cookie's flavouring

indicators.note: probing means the dialect word goes into the biscuit

parts.note: the Oreo is a sandwich biscuit with a cream filling
gan is the Newcastle dialect word for go

explanation.surface: A Newcastle native makes off with a biscuit's flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is someone from Newcastle upon Tyne, in north-east England, whose dialect uses 'gan' for the verb go.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a herb whose dried leaves are used to flavour food.

clue.text: Student, fooling around, regularly muddled geographical term

parts.note: L, for learner, is a student
at it means up to mischief, fooling about

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of muddled is taken

explanation.surface: A student messing about gets confused by a geography term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes UDE, the alternate letters of MUDDLED. 'muddled' looks like an anagram signal but is fodder for the alternation.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude is the angular distance north or south of the equator, a term from geography.

clue.text: Student outstanding at university — Oxford, maybe

parts.note: L, for learner, is a student
ace means excellent, outstanding
up means in residence at university, as in 'up at Oxford'

explanation.surface: An outstanding student at university, perhaps at Oxford.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford' looks like the university, but is a type of shoe; 'maybe' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An Oxford is a classic shoe fastened with laces, an example of a lace-up shoe.
